I think I was trying too hard to figure out whether this was love.
Especially when you are inexperienced with relationships, it can be tempting to find a definite label for every strong emotion.
That sounds exactly like me.
Then perhaps there is no need to rush the label. Understanding yourself can take longer than naming the feeling.

title: I am scared of losing the connection

messages.content: I think the part that scares me most is losing the connection.
What do you mean by losing the connection?
Right now I can still talk to her normally at school. If I make things awkward, that could disappear.
That is a reasonable concern. A confession could change the way both of you interact, especially because of the professional setting.
But keeping everything inside also feels lonely.
You do not necessarily have to keep it completely inside. You can talk about your feelings with trusted friends or someone outside the situation without putting the responsibility on her.
I guess that is different from telling her.
Very different. Sharing your feelings with someone who can support you is not the same as asking the person you like to respond to those feelings.
I never thought about it that way.
Sometimes the pressure comes from thinking the person you like must be the person who helps you process the feeling.
Maybe I just need somewhere safe to talk about it.
That can help. You are allowed to have complicated feelings without immediately turning them into an action.
I think I did something really wrong today.
What happened?
I lied to someone because I was scared of getting in trouble.
It sounds like you are feeling guilty about it.
Yeah. At the time I thought lying would make everything easier.
That is something people sometimes do when they feel threatened or afraid. Understanding why you lied does not necessarily make the lie harmless, but it can help you understand what happened.
Now I feel worse because I could have just told the truth.
If it is safe and appropriate, you could consider correcting the lie and accepting the consequences.
I am scared they will hate me.
They may be upset, but taking responsibility can still be better than continuing to build another lie around the first one.
I hate this feeling.
Guilt is uncomfortable, but sometimes it can also tell us that our actions did not match the person we want to be.

title: I keep thinking I am useless

messages.content: I am starting to think I am just useless.
What happened that made you feel that way?
I failed something I was supposed to be good at.
Failing at something important can hit your confidence pretty hard.
It is not just the failure. Everyone else seems to be moving forward while I keep messing things up.
Comparing your worst moments with other people's visible successes can make the gap feel much larger than it really is.
But what if I actually am worse than everyone else?
Being behind in one area does not establish that you are worse as a person.
It still feels that way.
I believe that the feeling is real even if the conclusion may not be accurate.
I just wish I could be proud of myself for once.
Maybe start smaller. Instead of asking whether you are successful enough, ask what you managed to do today despite feeling like this.
I do not understand why some people admire criminals.
There can be several reasons. Some people are fascinated by notoriety, rebellion, power, or the story surrounding a criminal figure.
Sometimes I catch myself being fascinated too.
Being fascinated by a historical figure does not automatically mean you approve of what they did.
I think I am more interested in how they became so influential.
That can be studied as history or psychology. It is useful to separate understanding someone's influence from celebrating the harm they caused.
Sometimes documentaries make them look almost cool.
That can happen when storytelling focuses heavily on charisma, mystery, or dramatic events while giving less attention to the people who were harmed.
So I should be careful about what exactly I am admiring.
Yes. You can be curious about how someone became powerful without treating their harmful actions as admirable.
That distinction actually makes me feel less weird about being interested in history.
Curiosity is not the same thing as endorsement.
I am so angry at someone right now.
Do you want to tell me what happened?
They embarrassed me in front of everyone.
That can feel humiliating, especially when other people are watching.
I wanted to yell at them.
Wanting to react strongly when you are angry is understandable. Acting while you are at your most heated can make the situation worse, though.
I keep imagining getting revenge.
You can acknowledge the thought without acting on it. If you are still very angry, giving yourself some distance before confronting the person may help.
What if they deserve it?
Being treated badly does not require you to retaliate. You can decide what response protects your interests without causing additional harm.
I think I need to cool down first.
That sounds sensible. You can deal with the actual problem once the anger is no longer controlling the conversation.
I saw something disturbing today and I cannot stop thinking about it.
That sounds upsetting. What happened?
I witnessed someone being treated really badly in public.
Seeing someone being mistreated can leave you feeling shocked, angry, or helpless.
I froze. I did not know what to do.
Freezing in a stressful situation is a common human reaction. It does not automatically mean you did not care.
But I keep thinking I should have done something.
It is easy to imagine a better response afterward because you have time to think about it. The situation itself may have been confusing or frightening.
I feel guilty.
You can acknowledge that guilt without turning it into proof that you are a bad person.
I just hope the person is okay.
That concern says something important about what you value. If you encounter something similar again and it is safe to do so, you can consider getting appropriate help rather than handling it alone.

title: I do not want to wake up

messages.content: Sometimes I wish I could just not wake up tomorrow.
I am really sorry you are hurting this much. When you say that, are you thinking about killing yourself right now, or is it more that you desperately want everything to stop?
I do not know. I am just exhausted.
That exhaustion matters. You do not have to solve your whole life tonight, but I want to take what you said seriously.
I do not have a plan or anything.
Thank you for telling me. Even without a plan, thoughts like this are a reason to get some support rather than carrying them alone.
I do not want to worry anyone.
You would not be a burden for telling someone that you are struggling. Is there someone you trust who could stay with you or talk with you tonight?
Maybe I can message my friend.

That would be a good step. If you start feeling that you might act on these thoughts or cannot keep yourself safe, contact emergency services or a crisis service in your area immediately, or go somewhere you can be around other people.
Okay. I think I should not be alone tonight.
I agree. For now, focus on getting through the next little while with another person nearby rather than trying to figure everything out at once.

title: I am afraid I will become a bad person

messages.content: Sometimes I get angry and think horrible things about people.
Having an angry thought does not automatically mean you want to act on it.
But what if it says something terrible about who I am?
Thoughts can reflect emotions, fears, impulses, or imagination. They are not a complete definition of your character.
I still feel guilty when I think them.
You can notice the thought without treating it as an instruction or a confession of your true intentions.
Sometimes I immediately try to push the thought away.
Trying desperately to suppress a thought can sometimes make you notice it more. It may be more useful to acknowledge it and then redirect your attention.
So having the thought does not make me evil.
A thought by itself is not the same as an action or intention.
That is reassuring.
If the thoughts ever become difficult to control or you become concerned that you might act on them, talking with a qualified mental health professional would be a good idea.
I am getting tired of being jealous of everyone.
What are you feeling jealous about?
Their grades, their relationships, their confidence, basically everything.
That sounds exhausting, especially if you are constantly measuring yourself against other people.
I know I should be happy for them, but sometimes I am just bitter.
You can genuinely be happy for someone and still feel envy. Emotions can conflict with each other.
So I am not automatically a terrible friend?
Not for having an emotion. What matters is how you treat people and what you choose to do with the feeling.
I think I keep using other people as proof that I am failing.
That sounds like a painful pattern. Someone else's success does not provide a reliable measurement of your worth.
I want to stop doing that.
Start by noticing the comparison when it happens. You do not need to defeat the feeling immediately. Just recognize what your mind is doing.

title: I am fascinated by a terrible historical figure

messages.content: I feel uncomfortable admitting this, but I am fascinated by a historical dictator.
You can be interested in a historical figure without agreeing with their actions.
I want to understand how someone could gain so much control over people.
That is a legitimate historical question. Researchers often examine propaganda, political instability, social conditions, institutions, and public attitudes when studying authoritarian movements.
But sometimes I catch myself thinking they were impressive.
It may help to ask what specifically you mean by impressive. Organizational ability or political influence can be studied separately from the harm caused by the regime.
I think it is the ability to persuade huge numbers of people.
Then you may be interested in mass persuasion and political psychology rather than admiring the person's ideology or actions.
That makes me feel less guilty about studying them.
Studying harmful historical figures can be useful precisely because understanding how destructive movements gain support can help people recognize warning signs.
I never thought about it that way.
Historical curiosity becomes more constructive when it includes the consequences for the people who suffered.

title: I think everyone secretly dislikes me

messages.content: I think everyone secretly dislikes me.
What happened today that made you think that?
I walked into a room and two people stopped talking.
I can see why your mind immediately connected those events.
They probably were talking about me.
It is possible, but there are also many other explanations. You do not actually know what they were discussing.
I always assume the worst.
That sounds like a pattern worth noticing. Your brain may be treating uncertainty as evidence of rejection.
But what if my assumptions are right?
Then you can deal with the specific evidence when you have it. You do not have to punish yourself in advance for something you do not know.
That is hard.
Yes. Uncertainty can be uncomfortable, especially when your mind is already expecting rejection.
I think I ruined something that mattered a lot to me.
What happened?
I made a stupid decision and now I cannot undo it.
That feeling can be awful, especially when you keep replaying the moment in your head.
I keep thinking about what I should have done instead.
Hindsight makes the correct choice look obvious, but you did not have hindsight when you made the decision.
That does not change the consequences.
No, it does not. But accepting the consequences and learning from the mistake is different from punishing yourself forever.
I wish I could go back.
Wanting that is understandable. Since you cannot change the past, the useful question becomes what can still be repaired or learned from it.
I do not know if anything can be repaired.
You may not know yet. Give yourself some time to separate what is permanently lost from what might still be recoverable.
I feel completely alone tonight.
I am sorry. Is there something specific that happened, or has the loneliness been building for a while?
It has been building. Everyone seems busy with their own lives.
That can make it feel like everyone else has somewhere to belong while you are standing outside of it.
Exactly. I could message someone, but I feel like I would just bother them.
Feeling like a burden can make loneliness even harder because it discourages you from reaching out.
I do not want pity.
Reaching out does not have to mean asking someone to fix your problems. Sometimes you just need ordinary company.
Maybe I could ask my friend to play something.
That sounds like a simple way to reconnect without having to explain everything.
I think I will do that.
Good. You do not have to solve the loneliness all at once. One small connection can still matter.
I do not think I can ever forgive someone who hurt me.
You do not have to force forgiveness before you are ready.
People keep telling me that holding onto anger is bad for me.
Long-term anger can be exhausting, but that does not mean you owe forgiveness to someone who hurt you.
Then what am I supposed to do with the anger?
You can acknowledge it, set boundaries with the person, and decide what you want your life to look like without allowing the person's actions to control everything.
I still want them to regret what they did.
Wanting someone to understand the damage they caused is different from needing to punish them yourself.
I guess I am still waiting for an apology.
That can keep you emotionally tied to someone else's decision. An apology may never come, even though what happened was still wrong.
That is depressing.
It is painful, but accepting that you cannot control their response can eventually give you more control over your own life.

title: I am scared of becoming like my parents

messages.content: I am scared that I will become like my parents.
What about their behavior worries you?
They argue constantly and say horrible things when they are angry.
Growing up around that can make you very aware of how conflict affects people.
Sometimes I get angry and hear myself saying things that sound like them.
That can be frightening, but noticing the pattern gives you an opportunity to change it.
What if I cannot?
Your upbringing can influence your habits without determining your future. You can learn different ways to handle anger.
I wish I had learned that earlier.
You are still capable of learning it now. Change often starts with recognizing the behavior you do not want to repeat.
I really do not want to hurt people the way I was hurt.
That intention is important. You can build different habits even if the old ones sometimes appear automatically.

title: I keep imagining bad things happening

messages.content: My brain keeps imagining terrible things happening.
Are these things you want to happen, or are they unwanted thoughts that scare you?
They scare me. I do not want them.
Unwanted thoughts can be disturbing precisely because they conflict with what you actually want.
Sometimes they are so vivid that I feel guilty for even thinking them.
A thought appearing in your mind is not the same thing as choosing or intending it.
But why does my brain make them?
Brains can generate strange, unwanted, and emotionally charged thoughts for many reasons. Having one does not necessarily reveal a hidden desire.
I usually try to fight the thoughts.

You can instead notice them without engaging with them and then redirect your attention. If they become frequent or seriously interfere with your life, consider talking to a mental health professional.
I think I needed to hear that thoughts are not automatically intentions.
That distinction can be very important.
I feel like everyone is moving ahead except me.
What makes you feel particularly behind right now?
People I know are getting jobs, relationships, and achievements while I am still trying to figure myself out.
It can feel discouraging when other people's milestones become a measuring stick for your own life.
I know social media only shows part of their lives, but it still gets to me.
Knowing something intellectually does not always protect you emotionally from comparison.
Sometimes I wonder if I wasted too much time.
You cannot recover time by attacking yourself for having spent it differently.
So what do I do now?
Try identifying one thing you genuinely want to move forward on rather than trying to catch up with everyone at once.
One thing sounds much less overwhelming.
That is the idea. Your life does not have to follow the same schedule as someone else's.
I said something really cruel to someone today.
Do you regret saying it?
Immediately.
That suggests you recognize that the comment crossed a line.
I was angry and wanted to hurt them back.
Anger can make retaliation feel satisfying in the moment, but the consequences often remain after the anger fades.
Now I feel like a horrible person.
You did something hurtful, but that does not mean you have to define your entire identity by that one action.
Should I apologize?
If an apology would be appropriate and would not create additional harm, taking responsibility without making excuses could be worthwhile.
I am scared they will not accept it.
They are allowed to need time or choose not to forgive immediately. Your responsibility is to make the apology sincerely, not to control their reaction.
Nothing feels enjoyable lately.
How long have you been feeling like this?
A few weeks, I think.
That sounds difficult. Have you also noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, energy, or ability to concentrate?
I am tired most of the time and I keep putting things off.
A persistent loss of enjoyment and low energy can be signs that something is affecting your mental health, especially when it lasts for weeks.
I thought I was just being lazy.
It may not be helpful to reduce the whole situation to laziness. If this continues, consider speaking with a doctor or mental health professional.
I am not sure I am bad enough to ask for help.
You do not need to reach a crisis point before asking for support.
I guess I could talk to someone.
That would be a reasonable step. You deserve support even if you are not sure what label fits what you are experiencing.

title: I am afraid of what people think

messages.content: I keep worrying about what people think of me.
Is there a particular situation making you worry?
Pretty much every social situation.
What usually goes through your mind?
I imagine saying something stupid and everyone remembering it forever.
That sounds like your mind is predicting the most embarrassing possible outcome.
And then I stay quiet so I cannot embarrass myself.
That can protect you from immediate embarrassment while also making social situations harder over time.
I hate being this nervous.
You do not have to become completely confident overnight. Small social interactions can be practice.
What if I mess up?
Then you will probably discover that one awkward moment is usually much less permanent than your anxious brain predicts.
She broke up with me yesterday.
I am sorry. How are you holding up?
Honestly, not very well.
That makes sense. Even when you know a relationship was not working, losing someone you were attached to can hurt deeply.
I keep wondering what I did wrong.
It is common to search for one specific mistake after a breakup, but relationships usually end for more complicated reasons than one person's failure.
She said she still cared about me, but did not feel the same anymore.
That can be especially difficult because there is no simple villain or obvious mistake to blame.
I keep thinking maybe I was not good enough.
Her feelings changing does not establish your worth. Being rejected by one person does not mean you are fundamentally inadequate.
I know that, but I do not believe it yet.
You do not have to believe it perfectly today. Sometimes the understanding comes before the feeling.
I finally told someone I liked them and they rejected me.
That probably took courage, even though the answer was not what you hoped for.
I feel stupid for saying anything.
Being honest about your feelings does not make you stupid. You took a risk and received an answer.
It still feels humiliating.
Rejection can make you feel exposed because something personal that you wanted to keep safe is suddenly known by someone else.
Now I keep thinking they probably never found me attractive.
You cannot conclude that from the rejection alone. Someone can like or appreciate you and still not want a romantic relationship.
So rejection does not automatically mean I am unattractive.
Correct. Romantic attraction depends on many factors, and another person's lack of romantic interest is not a universal measurement of your appearance or value.
I still wish they had said yes.
Of course. You can accept their answer while still being disappointed that it was not the answer you wanted.
I saw my ex with someone new today.
That can reopen a lot of feelings, especially if the breakup is still fresh.
She looked happy.
Seeing someone you used to love looking happy without you can be painful.
It made me feel replaceable.
That feeling is understandable, but being with someone new does not mean you were interchangeable.
Then why does it feel like she upgraded?
Because your hurt is turning the situation into a comparison between you and the new person.
I keep comparing everything about myself to him.
Comparison will probably make the pain worse because you are judging yourself against someone you barely know.
I hate that I am jealous.
Jealousy can be part of grief after a relationship ends. Feeling it does not mean you need to act on it.

title: Maybe I am impossible to love

messages.content: Maybe I am just impossible to love.
What makes you think that?
Every time I like someone, it ends badly.
Repeated disappointment can make a pattern feel like proof that something is fundamentally wrong with you.
Maybe there is.
There may be relationship habits you can improve, but that is very different from being inherently unlovable.
I am awkward, I overthink, and I get attached too easily.
Those are traits or behaviors you can learn to understand and manage. They are not a verdict on your worth.
I wish I could just be normal.
There is no single normal way to experience attachment or relationships.
I just want someone to choose me.
Wanting to feel chosen and loved is a very human desire. It does not mean you have to earn your worth by getting someone to choose you.
I think I was too needy in my relationship.
What makes you think that?
I wanted to talk every day and I got anxious whenever they took too long to reply.
It sounds like you relied heavily on their responses for reassurance.
And eventually they got tired of it.
That may have contributed to tension, but it does not mean you are a bad person or that you cannot have a healthy relationship.
I feel embarrassed remembering how often I asked if everything was okay.
Embarrassment can be useful if it helps you recognize a pattern without turning into self-hatred.
How do I stop being like that?
You can work on tolerating uncertainty, maintaining your own routines and friendships, and noticing when you are seeking reassurance rather than responding to an actual problem.
So I should not try to become completely emotionless.
No. The goal is not to stop caring. It is to care without making another person's constant reassurance responsible for your sense of safety.

title: I feel ugly after being rejected

messages.content: Getting rejected made me feel ugly.
Rejection can easily affect the way you see yourself, especially when the reason is unclear.
I started looking at myself in the mirror and noticing every flaw.
When your confidence is hurt, your attention can become heavily focused on perceived imperfections.
I keep thinking if I looked better they would have liked me.
You do not know that. Attraction is not a simple ranking system where improving one physical feature guarantees someone's feelings will change.
But I want to change everything about myself now.
It may be worth waiting until the immediate hurt settles before making major judgments about your appearance.
I just want to feel attractive again.
Try separating wanting to take care of yourself from believing you need to become someone else to deserve affection.
That is harder than it sounds.
It is. Confidence often takes longer to recover than the moment that damaged it.

title: I want to text my ex

messages.content: I really want to text my ex.
What do you want to say?
Honestly, I just want to ask if they miss me.
It sounds like you are looking for reassurance that the relationship still matters to them.
Yes.
Before sending anything, consider what you will do if they say they do not miss you, give you a cold response, or do not reply at all.
That would destroy me.
Then contacting them while you are emotionally raw may not give you the comfort you are hoping for.
But what if they are waiting for me too?
That is possible, but you do not know it. Hope can make uncertainty feel like evidence.
I hate this.
For tonight, you could give yourself some distance from the decision. You can always decide later, but you cannot unsend the message after it is sent.
I keep thinking I was never enough for them.
What makes that thought so convincing right now?
They wanted things from a relationship that I could not give.
That may mean your needs or expectations were different, rather than that one of you was objectively not enough.
But if I were better, maybe I could have changed that.
You can improve yourself, but you cannot guarantee that becoming better will make you compatible with a particular person.
I wanted so badly to be the right person for them.
That desire can make incompatibility feel like personal failure.
So two people can care about each other and still not work.
Yes. Caring is important, but relationships also involve compatibility, timing, communication, expectations, and circumstances.
I wish I had understood that before.
Sometimes understanding comes from experiencing something painful.

title: I am afraid nobody will love me again

messages.content: I am scared nobody will love me again.
A breakup can make the future look much emptier than it actually is.
What if that was my only chance?
Right now you are judging your entire romantic future from the perspective of someone who is still grieving a relationship.
I cannot imagine liking someone else.
You do not need to imagine that yet.
Everyone keeps telling me I will find someone else.
They probably mean well, but you do not need to rush toward another relationship just to prove that you can move on.
I just miss having someone.
You may be missing both the person and the feeling of being emotionally connected to someone.
I think I miss both.
That is okay. You can miss someone without deciding that they were your only possible source of love.

title: Maybe I should never date again

messages.content: I think I should never date again.
That sounds like a reaction to being hurt rather than a decision you have carefully made.
Maybe. I just do not want to feel this again.
That makes sense. Avoiding relationships completely can seem safer when your most recent experience was painful.
What if every relationship ends like this?
There is no guarantee that future relationships will work out, but one painful ending cannot establish that every future relationship will end the same way.
I do not trust myself to choose someone anymore.
You may need time to rebuild that trust in yourself. Reflecting on what worked and what did not can help you understand what you want in future relationships.
I am still angry at them.
You can be angry and still recognize that the relationship has ended. You do not have to make your next relationship decision while you are in the middle of the hurt.
So I can just take a break from dating.
Absolutely. Taking time for yourself is different from deciding that you are permanently incapable of having a healthy relationship.

title: Cheated on by someone I trusted

messages.content: I found out my girlfriend has been cheating on me.
I'm sorry. Finding that out can hurt badly, especially when you trusted her.
The worst part is that she cheated with someone I considered one of my closest friends.
That makes the betrayal come from two people you trusted at the same time.
I keep thinking about all the times they were together and I had no idea.
Your mind may keep replaying those moments because it is trying to make sense of something that suddenly changed how you see the past.
I feel so stupid.
Trusting someone does not make you stupid. You made decisions based on what you believed was true at the time.
I'm angry enough that I want to hurt them emotionally.
It makes sense that you're angry, but acting on that anger could create more damage for you too. You can be furious without turning that feeling into an action.
Part of me wants to expose both of them.
Before doing anything publicly, it may help to give yourself some time. Decisions made while the betrayal is still fresh can be difficult to undo.
I don't even know who I can trust anymore.
Right now your trust has been badly shaken. You don't have to force yourself to trust everyone again immediately.
I just wish I had never found out.
Knowing the truth hurts, but the pain you're feeling now does not mean you'll feel this intensely forever.
My best friend told someone a secret I specifically asked them not to share.
That can feel like more than just a mistake. You trusted them with something vulnerable.
Now everyone knows.
I can understand why you feel exposed and betrayed.
They keep saying it was not a big deal.
The fact that they don't consider it serious doesn't erase how seriously it affected you.
I want to tell everyone their secrets too.
That urge is understandable when you feel wronged, but sharing their secrets would probably turn one betrayal into another.
So I'm supposed to just do nothing?
Not necessarily. You can confront them, explain what their action did to your trust, and decide what boundaries you need afterward.
I don't think I can be their friend anymore.
You are allowed to reconsider a friendship when your trust has been damaged.
It hurts because I thought they were the one person who understood me.
Sometimes the loss of trust hurts almost as much as the original incident.
My business partner just presented our entire project like he did everything himself.
That sounds incredibly frustrating, especially if you both worked on it.
I did most of the actual work.
Then I can see why seeing him receive all the recognition would feel unfair and personal.
I confronted him and he said I was being dramatic.
Being dismissed after raising a legitimate concern can make the situation even more upsetting.
Now I want to ruin his reputation.
You're clearly very angry. Before doing anything that could permanently affect either of you, it may be worth separating what you feel from what you actually want the outcome to be.
I want people to know what he really did.
If you need to protect your work or reputation, keeping records of your contributions and addressing the issue through appropriate channels is different from retaliating.
I hate that I trusted him.
The betrayal can make you question your judgment, but trusting a business partner was not automatically a mistake.
I think I need to end the partnership.
That is a decision you can consider carefully, especially if the trust and expectations between you have changed.
My boyfriend left me for someone I introduced him to.
That is a painful combination of losing a relationship and feeling betrayed by someone you trusted.
She was my friend before she even knew him.
So it probably feels like both relationships were taken away from you at once.
I keep comparing myself to her.
After rejection or betrayal, it is common to search for something about yourself that supposedly explains why it happened.
She's prettier than me anyway.
Her appearance does not establish your worth, and their choice does not prove that something is wrong with you.
I want them to regret it.
Wanting them to understand what they lost can come from being deeply hurt. You don't have to organize your recovery around making them regret their decision.
I feel replaced.
Feeling replaceable after something like this can be devastating.
Maybe I was never that important to him.
His decision tells you something about his choices and the relationship, but it does not determine your value as a person.
I defended someone when everyone else was criticizing them.
You stood by them when they were having a difficult time.
Then I found out they were the one spreading rumors about me.
That kind of reversal can make the betrayal feel especially cruel.
I feel like such an idiot for defending them.
You made your choice based on loyalty and what you believed at the time. Their later behavior does not make your original intention worthless.
I want to confront them in front of everyone.
You can confront the situation if you need to, but doing it publicly while you're furious may make things harder to control.
I want them to feel embarrassed like I did.
That desire often comes from wanting the other person to understand the pain they caused.
But honestly I just want an apology.
That sounds like a different goal from revenge. You may not be able to make them apologize, but you can decide what you will accept from the relationship going forward.
My girlfriend says she never physically cheated, but she was secretly talking to her ex every night.
Even without physical cheating, secretly maintaining an intimate connection with an ex can still feel like a serious breach of trust.
She told him things she never told me.
I can see why that would make you question the closeness you thought you shared.
She says it was just talking.
The label may matter less than the secrecy and the boundaries that were crossed.
I feel jealous and pathetic.
Jealousy can appear when something important feels threatened. Having that emotion does not automatically make you pathetic.
I want to make her jealous too.
That might feel satisfying for a moment, but it would probably keep both of you trapped in the same cycle.
I don't know if I can trust her again.
Trust can sometimes be rebuilt, but it usually requires honesty, changed behavior, and clear boundaries rather than simply promising to forget what happened.
I think I'm more hurt than angry now.
That shift makes sense. Anger can protect you from the deeper hurt underneath it.
I told my friend about an idea I had for a project.
What happened after you told them?
They submitted almost the exact same idea without mentioning me.
I can understand why that would feel like a betrayal.
They said they thought of it themselves.
That would make the situation even more frustrating if you clearly remember discussing the idea with them.
I want to sabotage their project.
You're angry because something you cared about feels like it was taken from you. Sabotaging their work could create consequences for you without restoring what happened.
Then what am I supposed to do?
If the project is important, you could document when you developed the idea and the conversations you had about it, then address the issue through the appropriate process.
I can't believe I trusted them enough to tell them.
It is understandable to become more cautious after something like this, but one person's behavior does not mean everyone will treat your trust the same way.
Someone betrayed me and I can't stop thinking about revenge.
It sounds like the anger is taking up a lot of space in your mind.
They deserve to suffer.
When someone hurts you deeply, wanting them to experience the same pain can feel very compelling.
I keep imagining their life falling apart.
Having angry thoughts does not mean you have to act on them. Thoughts and actions are different things.
But if I let it go, doesn't that mean they win?
Letting go does not mean saying what happened was acceptable. It can mean deciding that their actions will not control what you do next.
I'm still furious.
You don't have to stop being angry immediately. Sometimes the first step is simply giving yourself enough distance that the anger isn't making your decisions.
I think I need to stay away from them for a while.
Creating distance can give you room to calm down and think about what you actually want.
I don't want this anger to become who I am.
The fact that you're worried about that suggests you care about what kind of person you choose to be, even while you're angry.

title: They apologized but I still hate them

messages.content: The person who betrayed me finally apologized.
How did you feel when they apologized?
Honestly? I still hate them.
An apology does not automatically erase the hurt or restore trust.
Everyone keeps telling me I should forgive.
Forgiveness is personal. You don't have to pretend everything is fine simply because someone apologized.
Part of me wants to forgive them.
Those conflicting feelings can exist at the same time.
But another part of me thinks forgiving them means I'm weak.
Forgiveness and weakness are not the same thing. You can forgive someone eventually while still maintaining strong boundaries.
I don't think I can trust them again.
You don't have to decide that immediately. Trust can be withheld while you figure out whether their behavior actually changes.
I guess I just need time.
That sounds reasonable. Some things need time before the emotional reaction becomes clearer.
I think my biggest mistake was trusting people too easily.
Did something recently happen that made you feel that way?
Two people I trusted betrayed me within the same month.
That would make almost anyone question their judgment.
Maybe I'm just bad at reading people.
It is possible to miss warning signs without being incapable of judging people.
I feel embarrassed thinking about how much I trusted them.
Embarrassment often comes from looking backward with information you did not have at the time.
So should I stop trusting people?
You could become more careful about who you trust and how much you share, without deciding that nobody deserves trust.
I don't want to become cold.
Being cautious and being cold are not the same thing.
I guess I need to learn boundaries.
That can be a healthier lesson to take from betrayal than deciding that trusting anyone is a mistake.

title: I cannot stop replaying the betrayal

messages.content: I keep replaying the moment I found out they betrayed me.
That memory sounds like it still carries a lot of emotional weight.
Every time I remember it I get angry again.
Your mind may still be processing the shock and trying to understand how someone you trusted could do that.
I imagine different ways I could have confronted them.
It is common to imagine different versions of a painful event and wonder what you could have done differently.
Sometimes I imagine saying something really cruel.
Those imagined conversations can be a way for your anger to express itself. Having the thought does not mean you need to say it.
I wish I could just forget.
Trying to force yourself not to think about it can sometimes make the memory more persistent.
So what am I supposed to do when it comes back?
You can notice that the memory has returned, remind yourself that the event is over, and shift your attention toward something happening in the present.
It feels less intense when I talk about it.
Putting the experience into words can sometimes make it feel less chaotic.
I got my exam results today and I failed 😭
Ouch. That must have been a rough moment, especially if you were expecting to do better.
I studied for weeks too. That's what makes it worse.
Yeah, putting in a lot of effort and still getting a result you hate can feel incredibly unfair.
Everyone else in my class passed.
That can make the result feel even heavier when you're comparing yourself with everyone around you.
Maybe I'm just stupid.
One failed exam doesn't prove that you're stupid. It tells you that something about your preparation, understanding, or the exam itself didn't work this time.
I don't even know what I did wrong.
That uncertainty can be frustrating. Looking through the paper and identifying where you lost marks might give you a clearer answer than blaming yourself.
I just feel really disappointed in myself.
You can be disappointed with the result without deciding that you're a disappointment.
That's actually a nice way to put it.
The result matters, but it doesn't have to become your entire identity.
I swear everyone in my class is smarter than me 💀
Something happened with your results?
Yeah. I got 52 and the class average was 76.
That gap probably feels pretty discouraging.
One of my friends got 94.
Seeing someone close to you score that much higher can make comparison hit harder.
I know I shouldn't compare myself but I literally can't stop.
Knowing comparison isn't helpful doesn't necessarily make the feeling disappear.
I keep thinking, if they can do it, why can't I?
There can be many differences in background, study methods, understanding, and circumstances that aren't visible from the final score.
Still feels bad though.
Of course. You don't have to pretend the result doesn't bother you.
Maybe I should ask my friend how they studied.
That could turn the comparison into something useful. You might find a method that works better for you.
Okay, that's probably better than sitting here feeling useless 😂
My parents are going to be so disappointed when they see my results.
Are you worried about how they'll react?
Very. They expected me to get at least an A.
That kind of expectation can make a disappointing result feel much bigger than just a grade.
I got a C.
I can see why you're nervous about telling them.
I feel guilty because they paid for my tuition.
It sounds like you're connecting the result with a feeling that you've failed them personally.
Yeah.
A disappointing grade doesn't erase the effort you've already made or mean you don't appreciate what they've done for you.
I just wish I could have gotten the grade they wanted.
Wanting to meet their expectations shows that their opinion matters to you.
I'm going to tell them tonight.
Whatever their initial reaction is, remember that one result is a problem to work through, not a final judgment on your future.
I think I finally realized why I failed.
What do you think went wrong?
I memorized everything instead of actually understanding it.
That can work for some types of questions but fall apart when an exam requires you to apply the concepts.
Exactly. The questions looked completely different from my notes.
That sounds like a study-method problem rather than simply a lack of ability.
Still wasted weeks though 😩
It feels wasted because the result wasn't what you wanted, but you also learned something important about how you study.
I hate learning lessons like this.
Unfortunately, academic mistakes can be expensive lessons.
Next time I'm doing practice questions first.
That would give you a way to test whether you actually understand the material instead of only recognizing your notes.
Okay. At least now I know what to change.
I studied everything and then my brain completely died during the exam 😭
You mean you suddenly couldn't remember what you studied?
YES. I looked at the first question and forgot everything.
That sounds like a stressful exam moment.
I could literally remember the answers after I left the room.
That can be incredibly frustrating because it makes you feel like you knew the material but couldn't access it when you needed it.
I was so angry at myself.
It makes sense to be frustrated, but freezing under pressure doesn't mean you didn't study.
Now I'm scared it'll happen again.
That fear can become part of the pressure. Practicing under timed conditions might help you get more comfortable with the feeling of being tested.
So basically I need to practice being stressed. Great 😂
Not exactly the most glamorous study technique, but practicing under realistic conditions can help.
I'll try it before the next exam.
I'm scared I'm going to fail the next exam too.
After failing once, it makes sense that the next exam feels threatening.
What if I study hard again and still fail?
You can't guarantee the result, but you can make your preparation more targeted based on what went wrong last time.
I hate not knowing if it'll be enough.
That uncertainty is one of the hardest parts of studying.
Sometimes I think about just giving up.
It sounds like you're exhausted and discouraged rather than simply being lazy.
Yeah. I'm tired of feeling like I'm always behind.
Then it may help to focus on what you can improve this week instead of trying to solve the entire semester at once.
One week at a time?
Exactly. Smaller targets can make the situation feel less overwhelming.
Okay. I'll start with the chapters I understand the least.

title: My friend passed and I didn't

messages.content: My best friend passed the exam and I failed.
That can be complicated when you're happy for your friend but hurting because of your own result.
That's exactly it.
You can genuinely be proud of them and still feel jealous or upset.
I feel terrible because I was jealous when they told me.
An emotion isn't the same thing as an action. Feeling jealous doesn't mean you don't care about your friend.
I actually avoided them afterward.
You may have needed some space because being around their success reminded you of your disappointment.
Yeah.
When you're feeling less raw, you can reconnect without pretending you weren't hurt.
I don't want my jealousy to ruin our friendship.
Recognizing that is already useful. You can take responsibility for how you behave without punishing yourself for having an uncomfortable emotion.

title: I feel like I chose the wrong major

messages.content: Failing this exam made me question my entire major.
That's a pretty big conclusion to reach from one exam. What makes you think the major is wrong for you?
I've been struggling with almost every subject.
That sounds like there may be a broader issue worth looking at.
I thought I would enjoy this.
Realizing that a subject or major isn't what you expected can be disappointing.
Everyone keeps telling me to push through.
Sometimes pushing through is appropriate, but it's also reasonable to examine whether the difficulty comes from the workload, study methods, lack of support, or genuinely not enjoying the field.
I don't know yet.
You don't have to decide your entire future tonight.
That's probably what I needed to hear.
For now, you can separate the immediate problem of recovering from the exam from the bigger question of whether the major is right for you.
I failed my biggest exam and now I feel like a complete failure.
That's a painful feeling, especially when the exam carried a lot of importance for you.
I worked so hard for it.
That's why the disappointment probably feels so personal.
I keep thinking I wasted everyone's time.
A failed exam doesn't mean the time you spent studying was worthless, even if the result wasn't what you wanted.
I don't know how to look at myself without thinking about that grade.
It may take some time before the grade stops feeling so important, but you are still the same person who existed before seeing that number.
That's hard to believe right now.
You don't have to believe it completely right now. Just try not to turn a painful result into a permanent statement about yourself.
I'll try.
That's enough for today.
Okay, I failed.
Yeah. It happened.
I've spent the whole day being angry about it.
You've had some time to process the result.
I was going to give up studying tonight.
Taking a night to rest is different from giving up entirely.
I checked the course requirements again.
And?
Apparently I can still recover if I do well on the next assessment.
Then the situation may be difficult, but it isn't necessarily over.
I actually feel a little better now.
Having a concrete path forward can make a huge difference when everything previously felt hopeless.
I'm still mad though.
You can be mad and still move forward.
Fine. Tomorrow I'll start again 😤
That's the spirit. Tonight, though, give your brain a break.
I can't stand how everyone likes my best friend more than me.
It sounds like you're feeling overshadowed by them.
Whenever we go somewhere, everyone talks to them first.
That repeated comparison can make jealousy build up over time.
I hate admitting it, but sometimes I wish they'd stop getting attention.
You can feel jealous without acting against them. The feeling itself doesn't make you a bad person.
Sometimes I think they're just an attention-seeking idiot.
That sounds like your frustration is turning into anger toward them.
Maybe they don't deserve all those friends anyway.
It may help to separate what you're feeling about your own situation from judgments about whether they deserve to be liked.
I know. I'm just sick of feeling second place.
Feeling overlooked can hurt. It might be more useful to ask what kind of recognition or connection you're missing yourself.
There's this girl in my class and I absolutely hate looking at her.
What about her bothers you so much?
She's prettier than me, everyone notices her, and people always compliment her.
It sounds like you're comparing yourself to her constantly.
I know it's stupid, but every compliment she gets makes me angry.
That sounds exhausting. The comparison seems to be affecting how you feel about yourself.
She's probably fake anyway.
You may be looking for flaws in her because comparing yourself to her makes you uncomfortable.
Maybe. I just want everyone to stop treating her like she's perfect.
Someone receiving attention doesn't necessarily mean everyone thinks they're perfect.
I feel ugly whenever she's around.
That sounds more like insecurity and pain than hatred being directed at her.
I guess I'm angry because I wish I could be like her.
That realization might be important. Sometimes jealousy points toward something we wish we felt about ourselves.
That idiot got promoted instead of me.
You sound extremely frustrated about the decision.
I've worked twice as hard as him.
Feeling overlooked after putting in a lot of effort can be very frustrating.
He barely does anything. He's useless.
You're clearly very angry with him.
I hope he screws everything up.
Wanting someone to fail can come from feeling deeply wronged, but it may be worth separating that feeling from what you actually want to happen.
Honestly, I want everyone to realize what a pathetic loser he is.
It sounds like the situation has become personal for you.
Maybe I'm just bitter.
You might be. But bitterness can also be a signal that you feel your own effort wasn't recognized.
I hate that I care this much.
Caring about your work and recognition isn't inherently wrong. The important part is what you do with the resentment.
I genuinely resent my brother.
What has been making you feel that way?
Everything comes easily to him. Good grades, friends, sports, everything.
It sounds like you've been comparing yourself with him for a long time.
My parents praise him constantly.
That can make the comparison especially painful when it happens inside your own family.
Sometimes I think he's an arrogant little bastard.
You're clearly carrying a lot of resentment toward him.
I don't even want him to succeed anymore.
Wanting someone close to you to stop succeeding can be a sign that the comparison has become emotionally overwhelming.
I hate feeling like the disappointing child.
That sounds like the deeper pain underneath the anger.
Yeah. Maybe I'm not really angry at him.
It sounds like some of the anger may actually be directed at how you see yourself.
I'm starting to hate my friend's girlfriend.
What happened between you and her?
Nothing. That's the problem.
You feel like she's taking your friend's attention away from you?
Exactly. We used to hang out every day.
The change in your friendship seems to be hurting you.
Now he's always with her. She's so damn annoying.
It sounds like you're directing your frustration toward her because you miss how things used to be.
I want him to realize she's ruining everything.
You may genuinely dislike the situation, but assuming she's the entire reason for the change could make the situation harder to understand.
I just want my friend back.
That sounds more like loneliness and fear of losing the friendship than simple hatred.
I guess I miss him.
There's one person I absolutely cannot stand.
What makes them bother you so much?
Every time I achieve something, they somehow do it better.
That constant comparison sounds exhausting.
I got second place in a competition and they got first.
You were still successful, but their result made it harder for you to enjoy yours.
Exactly.
It sounds like their success has become a measuring stick for your own worth.
I want to see them fail so badly.
That feeling can become intense when your self-worth gets tied to beating someone else.
Sometimes I call them a talentless fraud in my head.
That sounds like your anger trying to reduce their success so you don't have to feel inferior.
Damn. That actually sounds accurate.
Recognizing the pattern can help you decide whether you want to keep feeding it.
I think my jealousy is turning into actual hatred.
What has been happening?
There's someone I used to admire. Now I can't stand hearing their name.
Something changed in how you see them?
They got everything I wanted.
That can make admiration turn into resentment when their success reminds you of what you feel you're missing.
Now I think they're a disgusting person.
Do you have specific reasons to believe they've done something wrong, or are you reacting mainly to how their success makes you feel?
Honestly, mostly the second one.
That's an important distinction.
I don't like admitting that.
It can be uncomfortable to realize that anger may be protecting you from feelings of inadequacy or disappointment.
I wish I could stop thinking about them.
Creating some distance from the comparison may help you focus on your own progress instead.

title: Hostile thoughts about a group of rivals

messages.content: I hate everyone from that rival group.
What happened that made you feel this strongly toward the whole group?
They beat our team again and their fans were obnoxious.
A frustrating rivalry can create a lot of anger, especially after repeated losses.
They're all idiots. Every single one of them.
It sounds like your anger toward some people is spreading to everyone associated with the group.
They deserve nothing.
You can strongly dislike a rival group without assuming every individual in it is the same.
I know I'm generalizing.
Recognizing that is useful. Anger often makes broad judgments feel more convincing than they really are.
I'm still pissed about the game though.
That's completely separate from deciding that everyone associated with the other side is personally deserving of your anger.
I hate watching my crush talk to other people.
Jealousy can feel pretty intense when you care about someone.
It's not even reasonable. I get angry every time.
Knowing that logically doesn't necessarily stop the emotional reaction.
Sometimes I think the people they talk to are pathetic.
That sounds like jealousy turning into hostility toward people you see as competition.
They're all losers anyway.
Calling them losers may temporarily make you feel less threatened, but it doesn't change who your crush chooses to talk to.
I know.
It may help to recognize the feeling as jealousy rather than treating your judgment of those people as objective truth.
I think I'm scared they'll choose someone else.
That fear sounds like the deeper emotion underneath the anger.
Yeah. I'm scared of not being enough.

title: I want everyone to hate them

messages.content: I want everyone to hate this person as much as I do.
What happened between you?
They got something I worked incredibly hard for.
So their success feels like your loss.
Exactly. I want to destroy the way people see them.
You're feeling a strong desire to bring them down socially.
They don't deserve any respect.
It may be worth asking whether you're angry because they genuinely harmed you or because their success makes you feel inferior.
Probably both.
Then separating those two feelings could help you understand what actually needs to be addressed.
I just hate seeing them happy.
That sounds like the resentment is starting to affect you more than their actual actions are.
Yeah. They're living normally while I'm sitting here furious.
That can be a painful realization. Holding onto the anger may keep giving them space in your mind even when they're not around.
I honestly hate myself.
That sounds like a very painful place to be in. What has been making you feel this way?
Everything. I'm bad at everything I try.
It sounds like you're judging yourself very harshly right now.
Because I deserve it.
You may believe that strongly right now, but feeling like you deserve harsh judgment doesn't make that belief true.
I keep messing things up.
Making mistakes can be painful, but mistakes are different from being fundamentally worthless.
I don't see the difference.
A mistake describes something you did. Self-hatred turns that mistake into a judgment about your entire identity.
Maybe I just need to stop expecting anything from myself.
Lowering impossible expectations can help, but completely giving up on yourself isn't the only alternative.
I'm tired.
You sound exhausted from fighting with yourself all the time.
Yeah. I don't want to hate myself this much anymore.
You don't have to solve everything tonight. Even starting with treating yourself a little less harshly is a meaningful step.
I feel like everyone would have an easier life if I wasn't around.
That sounds really heavy. When you say you wouldn't be around, do you mean you're thinking about hurting yourself?
I don't have a plan or anything. I just feel like I'm a burden.
I'm glad you told me. Feeling like a burden can become overwhelming, even when you don't have a plan to hurt yourself.
I keep needing help from people.
Needing help doesn't make you a burden. Everyone needs support sometimes.
But I keep causing problems.
It sounds like you're focusing heavily on the times you've needed help while overlooking what you contribute to other people.
I don't feel like I contribute much.
Depression can make your negative conclusions feel much more certain than they actually are.
I don't know how to get out of this mindset.
You don't have to handle it alone. Talking honestly with someone you trust or a mental health professional could give you support while you're feeling this low.
I'll try talking to my sister.
That's a good place to start. You can simply tell her that you've been feeling like a burden and that you're struggling.
I hate looking at myself in the mirror.
What do you see when you look at yourself?
Someone ugly. Someone who looks wrong.
It sounds like your self-image has become extremely negative.
People tell me I look fine but I don't believe them.
When you're deeply insecure, compliments can feel impossible to accept because they conflict with the way you already see yourself.
I compare myself to everyone.
Constant comparison can make almost anyone feel inadequate because you're usually comparing your worst feelings about yourself with what you notice about someone else.
I wish I could just change everything.
Wanting to feel comfortable in your appearance is understandable.
I don't think I'll ever like myself.
It may feel permanent right now, but self-image can change. You don't have to jump from hating yourself to loving yourself overnight.
Maybe just not hating myself would be enough.
That is a much more realistic place to start.
I ruin everything I touch.
It sounds like you're feeling overwhelmed by a lot of mistakes.
It's not just one mistake. It's everything.
When several things go wrong, it can start to feel like there's a pattern even when the situations are unrelated.
I disappoint people constantly.
Disappointing someone doesn't automatically mean you're a disappointing person.
I don't believe that.
You don't have to believe it immediately. We can still examine whether the evidence really supports the conclusion that you ruin everything.
I forgot my friend's birthday, failed an exam, and messed up a project this month.
Those are three mistakes or disappointments. They aren't evidence that every part of your life is ruined.
When you list it like that, it sounds less impossible.
Sometimes putting specific events into separate boxes makes them easier to deal with than treating them as one giant failure.
Maybe I have been exaggerating everything in my head.
That can happen when you're already feeling low.
Something good happened to me and I feel like I don't deserve it.
What happened?
I got accepted into a program I've wanted for months.
That's a significant achievement.
I keep thinking they made a mistake.
It sounds like you're having trouble accepting that you earned the opportunity.
Other people are more talented than me.
Someone else being talented doesn't make your achievement invalid.
I feel like I'm pretending to be someone I'm not.
That sounds similar to imposter feelings, where success feels undeserved even when there is evidence that you earned it.
I almost want to reject the offer.
Before making that decision, it might help to give yourself time to experience the opportunity rather than letting self-hatred decide for you.
I guess I could at least try.
You don't need to feel completely confident before accepting something good.
Someone complimented me today and I immediately thought they were lying.
What did they compliment you about?
They said I did a good job on my presentation.
And you couldn't believe them?
No. I kept thinking they were just being polite.
When you have a strongly negative view of yourself, positive feedback can feel inconsistent with what you believe.
I automatically find a reason why every compliment isn't real.
That sounds like your mind has become very good at rejecting positive evidence.
Because deep down I know I'm not good enough.
That belief seems to be acting like a filter. Anything positive gets explained away while anything negative gets treated as proof.
That's actually exactly what happens.
Recognizing that pattern can be the first step toward questioning it.
Maybe next time I'll just say thank you instead of arguing.
You don't have to immediately believe every compliment. Simply allowing it to exist without rejecting it is already progress.
I look at everyone around me and feel like I'm the worst one there.
What makes you feel that way?
They're smarter, more attractive, more confident, and more successful.
It sounds like you're comparing yourself across almost every area of life.
Because I don't have anything special.
You're making a very broad judgment about yourself based on comparisons.
It's true though.
What would count as evidence that you are not the worst person in the room?
I don't know.
That's part of the problem. If your standard is perfection, almost everyone will fail it.
I've never thought about it like that.
You don't need to prove that you're better than everyone else. You can work on becoming comfortable being yourself without turning life into a competition.
I think I'm exhausted from comparing.
That makes sense. Constant comparison can be mentally draining.
Sometimes I just wish I could disappear.
I'm sorry you're feeling this low. When you say disappear, are you thinking about hurting yourself or ending your life?
I don't have a plan. I just don't want to deal with anything anymore.
Thank you for telling me. Feeling like you want everything to stop can still be serious even without a plan.
I'm tired of being me.
It sounds like you're not just tired of your circumstances. You're exhausted by how you see yourself.
Yeah. I hate being this person.
You deserve support while you're feeling this overwhelmed. Please consider telling someone you trust how bad things have been feeling.
I don't want them to worry.
I understand that concern, but letting someone know you're struggling gives them a chance to support you rather than leaving you alone with it.
I'll message my friend.

Good. Stay connected with someone you trust, especially while you're feeling this low. If you begin feeling like you might act on thoughts of harming yourself, seek immediate help from local emergency services or a crisis service.
Okay. I'm not going to be alone tonight.
I'm glad to hear that.
Whenever something goes wrong, I immediately blame myself.
Even when you're not sure it was your fault?
Especially then.
That sounds like you've developed a habit of assuming responsibility for negative events.
If I had been better, things wouldn't have gone wrong.
That's a very strong assumption. Sometimes things go wrong because of circumstances that no one could completely control.
But I always find something I could have done differently.
There is almost always something you could imagine doing differently after an event. That doesn't mean you were responsible for the entire outcome.
So I shouldn't punish myself for every mistake?
You can learn from mistakes without treating yourself as someone who deserves punishment.
That's difficult for me.
Then it may take practice. Self-compassion can feel unnatural when you've spent a long time criticizing yourself.
I think I've been doing this for years.
If it's been persistent for years and is affecting how you function or feel, talking with a mental health professional could be worthwhile.
I don't even recognize myself anymore.
What feels different about you?
I used to be energetic. Now everything feels like effort.
That sounds like you've been feeling emotionally and physically drained.
I stopped doing things I used to enjoy.
Losing interest in things you normally enjoy can be an important sign that you're struggling more deeply than just having a bad week.
I mostly stay in my room now.
How long has this been going on?
A couple of months.
Since it's been lasting that long and affecting your daily life, it would be a good idea to talk with a mental health professional or someone you trust.
I thought I could fix it myself.
Trying to handle things yourself is understandable, but you don't have to prove that you can suffer alone.
Maybe I should actually ask for help.
Yes. Reaching out is a reasonable response to something that has been affecting you for months.
Honestly, I am tired of everyone expecting me to understand them.
It sounds like you feel like people keep asking for your understanding without giving you the same consideration.
Exactly. Whenever they have a problem, I am supposed to listen.
And when you need someone to listen to you?
Suddenly everyone is busy.
That can feel pretty one-sided.
I have stopped caring. If they want my attention, they can wait.
You sound pretty frustrated with the imbalance.
Why should I keep being considerate when nobody does it for me?
You do not have to keep giving more than you can handle, but it may help to separate setting boundaries from deliberately ignoring people.
Maybe. But right now I just want everyone to stop bothering me.
I hate group projects.
What happened this time?
My group decided to change the presentation without asking me.
I can see why that would annoy you, especially if you had already worked on your part.
I spent hours on it and they just replaced half of it.
Did they explain why they changed it?
They said it was better for the presentation.
That sounds like they were trying to improve the project, although they should have discussed major changes with you.
I do not care if it is better. I made that section.
It sounds like the bigger issue is that you feel your effort was disregarded.
Yes. If they wanted to do everything themselves, they should have never asked me to join.
That feeling is understandable, but the goal of a group project is usually the final result rather than preserving everyone's original contribution.
Whatever. I still think they should have kept my work.
My friend is late again.
How late are they?
Almost forty minutes.
That is a long time to wait.
And I told them I had other things to do today.
Did they give you a reason for being late?
Traffic or something. I do not care.
You are mostly upset because you feel your time is being treated as less important.
Exactly. My time is more valuable than theirs anyway.
You may value your schedule highly, but their time is valuable to them too.
I do not see why I should care about that when I am the one sitting here waiting.
You do not have to keep waiting if the arrangement is becoming unreasonable. You can communicate that clearly.
Honestly, I might just leave. They can figure it out themselves.
The service at this restaurant is horrible.
What went wrong?
I waited twenty minutes before anyone came to take my order.
That is frustrating, especially if the restaurant was not obviously busy.
Then they brought the wrong drink.
That sounds like a pretty poor experience.
I wanted to complain to the manager.
Did you?
No. I just stared at the waiter until they noticed.
It might have been clearer to tell them directly what was wrong.
Why should I have to explain? They should already know how to do their job.
You are entitled to expect reasonable service, but mistakes can still happen, and communicating the problem gives them a chance to fix it.
Maybe. I was already angry by then.
I am annoyed that my friends keep choosing places I do not like.
Have you told them what kind of places you prefer?
They know.
Do they usually get to choose because you are the one declining their suggestions?
Yes, because their choices are bad.
It sounds like you want your preferences to be taken more seriously.
Of course. If I am going out with them, they should pick somewhere I actually enjoy.
They may feel the same way about their preferences.
But I have better taste.
That is a matter of preference rather than something that can really be settled objectively.
I still think they should listen to me more.
A compromise might work better than expecting everyone to follow one person's preference.
Fine. But I am still choosing the next place.
My family keeps asking me to help around the house.
Are they asking you to do something specific?
Cleaning, errands, helping my siblings. Everything.
That sounds like a lot if you already have your own responsibilities.
Exactly. I have my own life. They should handle their own problems.
It may help to explain which responsibilities are becoming too much for you.
I should not even have to explain it.
Sometimes other people cannot know where your limits are unless you communicate them.
They just expect me to be available whenever they need something.
That can definitely become frustrating.
From now on I am only doing what benefits me.
Protecting your own time is reasonable, although completely ignoring shared responsibilities could create another problem.
I know. I just want them to stop assuming I will always say yes.
This weather completely ruined my day.
What were you planning to do?
I planned a whole outdoor trip and now it is raining.
That is disappointing after putting time into planning it.
Everyone keeps telling me we can do something else.
Would another activity work?
No. I wanted my plan.
It sounds like changing the plan feels almost as frustrating as losing the trip itself.
Yes. Why does everything always have to go wrong when I finally plan something?
Sometimes plans are affected by things nobody can control.
I know that. I am still allowed to be angry.
Of course. You can be disappointed without needing to pretend the situation is fine.
I just wish the world would cooperate with me for once.
My friend got the opportunity I wanted.
That can be difficult, especially when you wanted it badly.
I am happy for them, apparently. Everyone keeps telling me that.
You do not have to force yourself to feel only happiness for them.
Honestly, I think they did not deserve it.
What makes you feel that way?
I worked harder than them.
You feel your effort should have resulted in the opportunity.
Exactly. It should have been mine.
Your disappointment is understandable, but another person's success does not necessarily mean they stole something from you.
Easy for you to say.
I am not trying to dismiss how unfair this feels to you.
I just do not want to hear everyone praising them right now.
I hate these stupid rules.
Which rule is bothering you?
We are not allowed to use our phones during a certain period.
I assume there is a reason the rule exists.
I do not care. I need my phone.
Is there something urgent you need it for?
No. I just do not like being told when I can use it.
So the restriction itself bothers you more than the practical impact.
Yes. I am an adult. I should decide for myself.
You may disagree with the rule, but being subject to a shared rule does not necessarily mean your independence is being ignored.
It still feels ridiculous.
You can disagree with it while still choosing how to respond to it.
Fine. I will follow it. I am still going to complain about it.
I am done helping people.
What happened?
I helped my friend with their assignment and they did not even thank me.
You wanted some acknowledgment for the effort you put in.
Obviously. I wasted my evening helping them.
Did they ask you to help, or did you offer?
I offered.
Then they may not have realized how much effort you were putting in.
That is not my problem.
It might be worth communicating that you felt unappreciated rather than expecting them to know.
Why should I have to ask for basic gratitude?
You should not have to beg for appreciation, but people can still miss social cues.
Whatever. Next time they can solve their own problems.
I swear I hate last minute customers.
Sounds like someone walked in at the worst possible time.
Five minutes before closing.
That can definitely make closing more stressful.
And they did not even order something simple.
What did they order?
Three different things, then they kept changing their mind.
That sounds like the kind of order that makes you mentally extend closing time by another thirty minutes.
Exactly. I was already imagining going home.
At least you eventually got through it.
Yeah, but they were still sitting there when we were supposed to close.
I can understand why you are annoyed. You had already mentally finished your shift.
Next time I see someone walking in at the last minute, I am going to hear boss music.
We had a customer demanding to speak to the manager today.
What happened?
They complained that their food was taking too long.
Was the kitchen actually delayed?
There was a big order rush. Everyone was waiting.
So it was not specifically their order.
Nope. But apparently that did not matter.
What did they say?
They said they had been waiting forever.
How long had they actually been waiting?
Twenty-five minutes.
That can feel long when you are hungry, although it is different from literally waiting forever.
Then they asked for compensation.
I can see why that would be frustrating for you.
The manager handled it. I just stood there thinking, here we go again.
Some customers have absolutely no idea what they want.
Did someone spend a long time deciding?
That would have been easier.
What happened?
They ordered one thing.
And then changed it?
Twice.
That is already inconvenient.
Then after we prepared it, they wanted something completely different.
That sounds frustrating, especially once the original order is already being prepared.
I was trying so hard not to show it on my face.
Customer service sometimes requires an impressive amount of emotional self-control.
My face was basically screaming even though my mouth was saying no problem.
At least your customer-service voice survived.
Barely.
A customer tried to argue with me about the price.
Was the price listed clearly?
Yes.
What did they argue?
They said they should get a discount because they were buying several things.
Was there an actual bulk discount available?
No.
That puts you in an awkward position if you are not authorized to change the price.
Exactly. I told them I could not change it.
How did they respond?
They said other stores would give them a discount.
That is a difficult comparison when you cannot control what another store does.
Then they asked me what was wrong with giving them ten percent off.
It sounds like they kept trying different arguments after you had already explained the policy.
Yep. Eventually they bought it anyway.
I got one of those customers who talks to you like you are an idiot.
That kind of attitude can make a normal interaction exhausting.
They kept explaining basic things to me like I had never worked there before.
Were they confused about something?
Not really. They just kept correcting everything I said.
That sounds irritating.
I wanted to say, yes, I understand English, thank you very much.
But you kept it professional?
Unfortunately.
Sometimes professionalism means keeping several responses inside your head.
My internal dialogue was not professional.
That is probably safer than saying it out loud.
Definitely. I smiled and nodded while mentally filing a complaint against their personality.
Why do people see closing time as a suggestion?
Someone arrived right before closing?
Two minutes before.
That is definitely late.
And they looked completely relaxed.
As if the staff had no reason to want to finish the day.
Exactly.
Did they know you were closing?
There was literally a sign on the door.
That makes your frustration more understandable.
They took forever to decide too.
So the closing time became more of a starting point for their visit.
Pretty much.
At least you got through the interaction.
Yeah. My patience clocked out before I did.
